q: 151. Which of the following SAARC country with highest population density?
explain: Maldives, being a small island nation with a concentrated population (especially in Male), has the highest population density among SAARC countries.

q: 152. Which of the following SAARC country with highest population literacy rate?
explain: Maldives has the highest literacy rate among SAARC nations, close to universal literacy.

q: 153. Which SAARC country has accepted the policy of dual Citizenship?
explain: Bangladesh permits dual citizenship for its nationals under specific conditions, unlike most other SAARC states.

q: 154. What is the currency of the 'Republic of Maldives'?
explain: The official currency of the Maldives is the Rufiyaa.

q: 155. Which is the first SAARC country to provide e-passport to its citizens?
explain: The Maldives was the first SAARC country to introduce e-passports for its citizens.

q: 156. From which country, the concept of the rural Development bank was emerged?
explain: The rural development bank concept, notably the microfinance-based Grameen Bank model, originated in Bangladesh.

q: 157. How many land-locked countries are there in South Asian Association for Regional Co-Operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has 3 land-locked countries: Nepal, Bhutan, and Afghanistan.

q: 158. How many water-locked countries are there in South Asian Association for Regional Co Operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has 2 water-locked (island) countries: Sri Lanka and Maldives.

q: 159. What is the Currency of Bhutan called?
explain: Bhutan's official currency is the Ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian Rupee.

q: 160. How many times that the SAARC summits held in Nepal?
explain: Nepal has hosted SAARC Summits three times: the 3rd (1987), 11th (2002), and 18th (2014) Summits, all held in Kathmandu.

q: 161. What percentage of total expenditure of SAARC secretariat is bear by Nepal?
explain: As per this reference, Nepal bears 10.72% of the total expenditure of the SAARC Secretariat, based on the organization's cost-sharing formula.

q: 162. Among the following South Asian Counties, Nepal first established diplomatic relation with:
explain: Among the given options, Nepal's diplomatic relationship with Afghanistan predates its ties with the other listed countries.

q: 163. When was BIMSTEC established?
explain: BIMSTEC was established on 6 June 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration.

q: 164. Which country is not the founder member of the BIMSTEC?
explain: BIMSTEC was founded in 1997 by Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand; Nepal joined later, in 2004, along with Bhutan.

q: 165. BIMSTEC permanent Headquarter at Dhaka was established on --------
explain: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat in Dhaka was formally established on 13 September 2014.

q: 166. Where is BIMSTEC permanent secretariat located?
explain: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

q: 167. Where was the 4th BIMSTEC summit held in 2018 A.D.?
explain: The 4th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal in August 2018.

q: 168. Who is Current 4th Secretary General of BIMSTEC?
explain: As per this reference material, Indra Mani Pandey is listed as the 4th Secretary-General of BIMSTEC.

q: 169. Which of the following statement is/are correct?
options: Nepal was granted the observer status of BIMSTEC in 1998
In 2018, it was expanded to embrace two more sectors including blue economy and mountain economy
Now, it has 7 areas of cooperation
explain: All three statements are correct: Nepal held observer status before becoming a full member, the sectors were expanded in 2018, and BIMSTEC now has 7 broad areas of cooperation.

q: 170. Which of the following is not the member state of BIMSTEC?
explain: BIMSTEC's seven members are Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan; Malaysia is not a member.

q: 171. When did Nepal formally get membership of BIMSTEC?
explain: Nepal formally became a member of BIMSTEC in February 2004.

q: 172. Currently, which country is the chair of BIMSTEC?
explain: As per this reference material, Bangladesh currently holds the chairmanship of BIMSTEC.

q: 173. What is the regional initiative comprising 7 member states of both SAARC and ASEAN called?
explain: BIMSTEC brings together countries bridging South Asia (SAARC) and Southeast Asia (ASEAN) around the Bay of Bengal.

q: 174. How many sectoral area of cooperation are indentified by the fifth BIMSTEC Summit held in Columbo, Sri Lanka?
explain: The 5th BIMSTEC Summit, held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, streamlined cooperation into 7 broad sectoral areas.

q: 175. Which Prime Minister of Nepal attended the 6th BIMSTEC Summit?
explain: K.P. Sharma Oli represented Nepal as Prime Minister at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit.

q: 176. 6th BIMSTEC summit was concluded in Bangkok with signing and inception of ___ points.
explain: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok concluded with the signing/adoption of an 18-point declaration/outcome document.

q: 177. What is the theme of 6th Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Summit?
options: Towards a Peaceful, Prosperous & Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region
Prosperous Economies, Healthy Peoples & Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region
explain: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok (2025) was held under the theme 'Prosperous, Resilient, and Open BIMSTEC'.

q: 178. At the conclusion of the 6th BIMSTEC summit, ___ took over as chair nation of BIMSTEC.
explain: Bangladesh assumed the BIMSTEC chairmanship at the conclusion of the 6th Summit in Bangkok.

q: 179. Which country was hosted the sixth BIMSTEC Summit in 2025?
explain: Thailand hosted the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in 2025.

q: 180. Which sector of BIMSTEC is leading by Nepal?
explain: Nepal is designated as the lead country for the People-to-People Contact sector within BIMSTEC's sectoral cooperation framework.

q: 181. Match the list I with II and select the correct answers from the given Codes: a.Trade & Investment b.Tourism c.Agriculture d.Security / 1.Nepal 2.Myanmar 3.India 4.Bangladesh
explain: Under BIMSTEC's lead-country arrangement: Bangladesh leads Trade & Investment, Nepal leads Tourism, Myanmar leads Agriculture, and India leads Security — matching a4, b1, c2, d3.
